question: The new EU steel market protection mechanism, in force since 1 July 2026, aims to protect EU industry from the effects of global overcapacity and import pressure. Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1457 sets out the distribution of tariff quotas, taking into account the specific situation of Ukraine and ensuring its preferential access.

In 2025, when Ukraine benefited from an exceptional exemption from the EU’s safeguard measures, Ukrainian steel exports to the EU increased by 30%, with around 46% of deliveries going to Poland. In the case of rebars the figure was around 70%. The current allocation, however, is based on 2022-2024 trade flows. In view of the requests to increase quotas for Ukraine: 1.
Is the Commission considering increasing the tariff quotas for Ukrainian steel beyond the levels set out in Regulation (EU) 2026/1457?

If the allocation of quotas is updated, will the Commission maintain the methodology based on 2022-2024 trade flows and not use the exceptional level of imports from 2025 as a basis for increasing quotas for Ukraine?

How will the Commission ensure that updating or increasing the quotas for Ukraine does not weaken the protection of the EU steel market, particularly in countries most vulnerable to an increase in imports, such as Poland?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.10.2026) Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/14571 distributes the tariff-rate quotas (TRQs) opened under Regulation (EU) 2026/13842 of the European Parliament and of the Council addressing the negative trade-related effects of global overcapacity on the EU steel market and amending Regulation (EU) 2020/21703.
The Commission is empowered to distribute these TRQs by taking into account the EU interest and, as applicable, the criteria set out in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384.

One of these criteria (i) is the consideration of ‘the situation of a Union candidate country facing an exceptional and immediate security situation, in particular where it previously benefitted from preferential access to the Union steel market’. The Commission has a continuous empowerment under Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 to adopt Implementing Regulations distributing quotas in line with these criteria.

This implies that, should a change linked to one of these criteria occur, the Commission could consider a new TRQs distribution. In doing so the Commission will carefully balance all the relevant criteria set in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 when distributing TRQs in the future.
